title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face for $13bn as the Open-Source AI Race Becomes a Control Point
subhead: Nvidia's $12.93bn acquisition of Hong Kong rival-free developer platform Hugging Face, combined with tech chiefs' pushback against AI regulation at the G20 and a new US open-source bill, signals the open-weight model ecosystem is now the battleground in the US-China AI race.

sections.heading: Nvidia Bets $13bn That Open Models Are the Future of AI
sections.body: Nvidia will acquire the developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, one of its largest acquisitions, betting that support for open AI models will drive demand even as its biggest customers build their own chips, Reuters reports. Under the deal, Nvidia pays about $11.9 billion to Hugging Face investors with up to $1 billion in equity retention for employees. CEO Jensen Huang stressed that 'Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem' and that Nvidia chips would not be required to build or deploy through it. Hugging Face was valued at $4.5 billion in its last disclosed round in August 2023, when it raised $235 million from Salesforce, AMD and Amazon. Nvidia exited its July quarter with $22.44 billion in cash, more than double January's $10.61 billion.
sections.whyItMatters: The deal positions Nvidia as the infrastructure layer for open-weight models — the counter to OpenAI and Anthropic's closed systems — and gives it direct visibility into how developers use rival models, useful intelligence as it chases top US and Chinese labs.

sections.heading: US Tech Chiefs Fight Regulation as G20 Hosts the AI Debate
sections.body: At a G20 Innovation Ministerial summit in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Tesla's Elon Musk pressed global powers to curb AI regulations, the South China Morning Post reports. Speaking alongside US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Huang urged policymakers to target 'actual and pragmatic harm' rather than 'hypothetical theoretical harm,' warning that 'the worst outcome is that you don't take advantage of it, that you are left behind.' Musk told a Tuesday session countries should make new technologies 'default legal as opposed to default illegal.' The pushback comes as Washington moves to ease regulation for domestic developers and executives lobby against potential bans on open-weight models. China's Science and Technology Minister Yin Hejun used the same forum to urge global AI cooperation rather than rivalry, ahead of the Xi-Trump summit.
sections.whyItMatters: Both superpowers are using a multilateral stage to frame the AI rules debate in their favor — Washington pushing deregulation as a competitiveness tool, Beijing countering with a cooperation narrative as it escalates spending.

sections.heading: US Congress Advances an Open-Source AI Leadership Bill
sections.body: The US House of Representatives advanced the Open-Source AI Leadership Act (H.R. 10152), which would direct the Department of Commerce to identify barriers to adopting US open-weight models and compile data on their adoption relative to Chinese ones, SCMP reports. The bill responds to a structural imbalance: most leading US models (OpenAI's GPT, Anthropic's Claude) are closed-source, while most leading Chinese models are released as open-weight. It was one of several proposals marked up in the House targeting China amid escalating tech competition.
sections.whyItMatters: Washington is treating open-weight adoption as a national-security and competitiveness metric, effectively moving to compete with China on the same open-model terrain it has long dominated — while US companies now race to control that distribution layer.

sections.heading: China's AI Buildout: ByteDance Megacluster and Moonshot IPO
sections.body: ByteDance, TikTok's parent, is in preliminary talks to add five to six gigawatts of AI compute in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia over the next two years, an SCMP exclusive reports, targeting delivery by early 2028. Based on Soochow Securities' estimate of roughly 160 billion yuan (US$23.8 billion) per gigawatt, the cluster could cost 800 billion to 960 billion yuan. The move comes as ByteDance reportedly secured a US$29.6 billion loan from a group of banks, the second-largest dollar-denominated loan in Asia this year. Separately, Moonshot AI — developer of the Kimi K3 open-weight model with more than 2.8 trillion parameters — has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO, targeting a listing as early as Q1 2027 and a final financing round valuing it around US$50 billion, SCMP reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Chinese AI champions are converting open-weight momentum into capital and compute at scale — a two-track hedge of domestic compute expansion and public-market fundraising that is reshaping the competitive map against US labs.

sections.heading: Frontier Gap Reopens: Anthropic's Fable 5.1 Widens the Lead
sections.body: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 took the global top spot on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index with a score of 66, six points clear of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 and Z.ai's GLM-5.3, the SCMP reports. It also claimed first place on Vals AI's index for complex real-world tasks across finance, coding and law. One Databricks staffer called the capability leap 'insane,' while observers said it undercut claims that Chinese open-weight developers had closed the gap with the frontier — though a stark price gap highlights the divergent strategies, Chinese models competing on cost while US labs push capability.
sections.whyItMatters: After weeks of Chinese open-weight momentum, the latest benchmark round favors US frontier labs — but the cost differential keeps Chinese models commercially relevant, especially for businesses balking at premium deployment bills.

sections.heading: Memory and Japan: Kioxia, SK Hynix, ASML Push Deeper Into AI Chips
sections.body: Japan's Kioxia outlined plans Thursday to use enhanced NAND flash memory as an alternative to DRAM, via a CXL module now under client review, to strengthen ties with US tech firms and fend off Chinese rivals, Nikkei Asia reports. ASML Japan plans to raise its domestic workforce to about 700 from 500 by 2030, supporting advanced chip production by Rapidus and TSMC in Japan. The buildout context: SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung has said he sees 'no signal' of oversupply and expects the memory shortage to last until the end of 2030, arguing memory chips are 'no longer just commodities' in the AI era.
sections.whyItMatters: Japan is quietly reinforcing its position in the AI chip supply chain on multiple fronts — memory differentiation against Chinese rivals and EUV tooling support for next-gen foundries — even as the broader memory market is expected to stay tight for years.

bottomLine: Today's developments mark a turn in the US-China AI race from raw model performance toward control of the open-weight ecosystem and its financing. Nvidia's $12.93bn purchase of Hugging Face, coupled with Huang and Musk's anti-regulation push at the G20 and a new US open-source leadership bill, signal Washington's core players are moving to shape the distribution layer where Chinese open models have won ground. Meanwhile China answered with compute (ByteDance's 5-6GW Inner Mongolia cluster) and capital (Moonshot's Hong Kong IPO), and memory players extended the buildout. The frontier benchmark gap briefly reopens in Anthropic's favor, but the strategic contest is now over platform, price and infrastructure as much as model quality.
sources: Reuters (via Nikkei Asia), South China Morning Post, Nikkei Asia, Bloomberg (loan figure cited by SCMP), Artificial Analysis via SCMP, Vals AI via SCMP, Soochow Securities via SCMP
